## Upgrade notes

- **From 1.2.4 or older, start any 1.3.x release once before you upgrade.** That start moves the blobs of keys with `..` or `\` to their new path. 1.4.0 no longer does this: those objects cannot be read, and the weekly orphan cleanup can delete their blobs.

The first start runs database migrations: job schedules, job settings, an audit log index and a table for data protection keys. On PostgreSQL it also installs the `pg_trgm` extension. Back up the database before you upgrade.

- **Everyone signs in again once.** The data protection keys now live in the database. Before, the container kept them in memory, and every restart signed everyone out.
- **The container runs as the user `app` (UID 1654), never as root.** Existing volumes keep working, because the old image gave `/data` to this user. A new bind mount needs `chown -R 1654:1654` on the host first. See [Container user](https://github.com/centrolabs/ObjeX/blob/v1.4.0/docs/configuration.md#container-user).
- **The container writes no log file.** It logs to stdout; read the logs with `docker logs` or `kubectl logs`. Set `Log__FilePath` to write a file again.
- **The compose files and the Helm chart use a read-only root filesystem.** `/tmp` is a `tmpfs` or an `emptyDir`. The chart sets the user in `podSecurityContext` and `securityContext`.
- **Browser uploads go to `PUT /api/upload` on the UI port.** Before, the bytes went through the SignalR connection. Behind a reverse proxy, raise the request body limit for the UI host too. nginx refuses bodies over 1 MB by default (`client_max_body_size`).
- **PostgreSQL: object search uses a trigram index.** ObjeX builds it in the background after each start when it is missing. It takes 40 to 200 MB per million objects. Without the right to create extensions, search scans the table and the log names the SQL statement to run. `Search__TrigramIndex=false` turns the index off. See [PostgreSQL search index](https://github.com/centrolabs/ObjeX/blob/v1.4.0/docs/configuration.md#postgresql-search-index).
- **A fourth weekly job recounts the bucket statistics**, Sunday 06:00 UTC. The Admin changes all job schedules on the Jobs page.

## Security fixes

- **A user could list, preview and delete objects in another user's bucket** after a navigation inside the web UI. The Objects page skipped the owner check when only the bucket in the URL changed. Affects 1.2.3 to 1.3.0.
- **The login page redirected a signed-in user to any `returnUrl`**, also to another host. A return URL with a tab or newline also left the site.

## Highlights

- New web UI: own component library, light and dark design tokens, a sidebar that collapses and resizes
- Jobs page: recurring jobs, recent runs, run details with the error, Run now, Retry and Delete
- Job schedules and settings in the browser: daily, weekly or cron, in your time zone
- Browser upload over HTTP: files and folders by picker, drop or paste, three at a time, with progress, cancel and retry
- Command palette (⌘K or Ctrl K) for pages, buckets, actions and objects; a bucket switcher in the breadcrumb
- Search by words in any order; on PostgreSQL in milliseconds with the trigram index
- Object list by keyboard, Shift-click ranges, preview paging with the arrow keys
- Preferences per browser: theme, compact rows, system font, 12-hour clock, relative times, start page
- Users page: search, filters, bucket count and last activity
- Quotas and bucket statistics stay exact under parallel uploads
- Sign-ins survive a restart
